name: Google Antigravity

surfaces.label: Antigravity CLI: agy, a single Go binary (also runs headless with -p; also serves the local language server)
Antigravity 2.0 desktop app (agent command center), Antigravity.app
Antigravity IDE standalone, Antigravity IDE.app (VS Code style editor with agent panel). The bundle name contains a space, see notes
Python SDK: google.antigravity spawns the Go 'localharness' binary as a child

working_signals.meaning: The per-conversation SQLite file is in WAL mode, so the live signal is the mtime of conversations/<id>.db-wal, not the .db (the CLI checkpoints on exit). The per_session glob ends in .db* so the probe's newest-mtime pick includes the -wal file. Write cadence during streaming or a long tool run is unmeasured; a stale file may not mean idle.

Inferred. Changelog v1.1.20 fixed a spinner loop that kept ticking after turn completion 'eliminating idle CPU wakeups', so idle agy should sit near 0 percent. The same agy process also hosts the local language server and Remote Control tunnel, so an idle agy is not guaranteed silent. Floor is a guess. On the IDE the process tree includes the persistent language_server_macos_arm child, and a forum bug report (discuss.ai.google.dev, 'High CPU Usage (400%) by language_server_macos_arm') shows it can burn CPU with no agent turn, so tree_cpu on the IDE is a weak signal.

waiting_signals.meaning: True while a tool confirmation dialog is showing. Exact and documented, but only reachable if the user configures statusLine in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json to a command that writes the payload somewhere; no file or process trace otherwise. agy runs the command on every agent state change and pipes JSON on stdin.

One of idle, thinking, working, tool_use, initializing. There is no 'waiting' value; waiting shows up in tool_confirmation_pending and pending_input_count (queued user messages). The same payload feeds the custom terminal title script (settings.json 'title').

Only gating event. The hook itself returns decision allow, deny, ask, force_ask or deny_unless_prior_grant. Per the hooks doc, ask prompts the user but respects Always Allow grants, so it may not prompt; force_ask always prompts. A hook returning force_ask (or ask on a not-yet-granted call) marks 'about to prompt the human'. There is no Notification event, so built-in permission prompts that no hook triggered cannot be seen by hooks.

Input field fullyIdle: true when the agent is finished and all background commands are done, false while background tasks still run. Best documented 'turn over' event, and the only one that separates 'model stopped' from 'background work still running'.
Opt-in (default false). System desktop notification plus terminal bell when a long-running task completes or needs attention. Terminal and OS side only.
agy -p --output-format json reports status WAITING when the run ended while waiting on input. Ended runs only, not a live signal.

hooks.config: hooks.json: workspace .agents/hooks.json, global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, or inside an installed plugin's hooks.json. The CLI also reads a 'hooks' block in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. Same file format for 2.0, CLI and IDE. Inspect with /hooks in the TUI. Command hooks only, JSON on stdin and stdout, camelCase, default timeout 30 s. Custom Markdown agents can list hook files in front matter.

telemetry.how: The CLI has no documented OpenTelemetry exporter. Feature request google-antigravity/antigravity-cli#366 is open; a reporter set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and friends on agy --print and saw nothing sent. Not checked for the 2.0 app or the IDE. settings.json 'enableTelemetry' is Google's own collection, not OTLP. The Python SDK (google-antigravity 0.1.5+) does emit OpenTelemetry GenAI spans, see examples/deep_dives/observability_otel.py in google-antigravity/antigravity-sdk-python. Community route for the CLI: a PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hook script that emits OTLP (e.g. danistrebel/agy-hooks).

Observed on agy 1.1.24 and 1.2.1 by third parties. Not vendor-documented.

notes: Not installed here; nothing was run. Verification 2026-09-29: power_assertion removed from working_signals because the IDE holds a NoIdleSleepAssertion for its whole lifetime (user report), which would read as always working. Remaining working signals (transcript_write on .db-wal, tree_cpu) are inferred and unmeasured, and so is the session-store mapping, hence documented is the ceiling and only for identity, hooks, statusLine and flags. Known false positive: a transient agy-ide / antigravity-ide CLI wrapper run may match the ide surface. The ide surface's path_contains '/Antigravity' is broad by design and relies on args_contain. Four surfaces share ~/.gemini but have separate data dirs: CLI ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli, 2.0 app ~/.gemini/antigravity, IDE ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide, sidecars under ~/.gemini/antigravity/sidecar_data. Config: ~/.gemini/config/{hooks.json,mcp_config.json,config.json,sidecars/,plugins/}. (1) agy is NOT Gemini CLI: Go binary named agy, not node, and a different store than ~/.gemini/tmp/*/chats. Do not let the gemini-cli row and this row overlap. (2) The row's session_store and per_session cover the CLI only. For the 2.0 app and IDE, the documented mirror is <app_data_dir>/brain/<conversationId>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl and a hook or statusLine script is the only documented way to learn the id; the 2.0 and IDE primary stores were not determined. (3) A plain agy launch has no id in argv; map it by cwd through ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/cache/last_conversations.json (inferred) or by lsof of the open conversations/<id>.db-wal (inferred, unverified). (4) 'Antigravity IDE.app' has a space: ps prints the path unquoted, and the probe splits args on spaces, so argv[0] arrives as '/Applications/Antigravity' and the rest as 'IDE.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron' (the IDE main executable is named Electron, per third-party reports; the 2.0 app's is Antigravity). The IDE surface is written to match under both a space-splitting parser and a full-path detector; the 2.0 surface path_contains '/Antigravity.app/Contents/MacOS/' cannot match the IDE. Electron helper processes are excluded by the same test. (5) The IDE runs a child language_server_macos_arm (Contents/Resources/app/extensions/antigravity/bin/, seen in a real ps line); the 2.0 app also has an app-local language_server, name and path unverified. Either is a persistent child that must not count as tool_children; that is why tool_children is left out. MCP servers and daemon background tasks are also persistent children. (6) agy remote-control start installs a LaunchAgent, so an always-on headless agy can exist with no terminal; it is idle unless a remote conversation is running. Its argv was not determined, so it is matched by the tui surface. (7) agy -p runs are matched and are simply working for their lifetime. (8) Conversation summaries.db has a not_fully_idle column and Stop has fullyIdle: the engine tracks 'idle' and 'fully idle' separately, so a turn can end while background tasks run. The column is community-observed, not documented, and this schema has no signal type for reading a database. (9) Versions seen 2026-09-29: CLI 1.2.13 (manifest, cask) vs 1.2.11 (download page), 2.0 app 2.18.1 (page) vs 2.17.0 (cask), IDE 2.5.5.
